title: sutra_signal_chains / sutra_trace — entry-point traversal
description:
Forward and backward traversal of the call graph from entry points to arbitrary symbols. Subsumes the original fallow "trace" idea and adds explicit entry-point modeling.

**Entry-point detection (rule-based):**
- Rust: `fn main`, `#[test]`, `#[tokio::main]`, `#[wasm_bindgen]`, public items in `lib.rs`, `#[bench]`
- Dart: `void main()`, route handlers, test bodies

**Tool shape:** `sutra_trace(symbol, direction=forward|backward)` → chains. For dead-code explanation: prove no path from any entry-point reaches X.

Call graph already exists; entry-point detection is a small per-language rule list; traversal is BFS with cycle detection.

**Output rendering needs a bit of design** — single canonical shape: top-N shortest paths to/from entry points, configurable N, cycles marked. Iterate from there. See "Trace output format" in docs/feature-ideas.md.

See docs/feature-ideas.md → "sutra_signal_chains / trace".

acceptance_criteria.text: Entry-point detection rules implemented for Rust and Dart
sutra_trace(symbol, direction=forward) returns chains from entry points to symbol
sutra_trace(symbol, direction=backward) returns chains from symbol to leaves
Cycles detected and marked, not silently truncated
Top-N path limit configurable; default chosen and documented
